Insurance: Check-ups and cleaning are the treatments most often included when a plan has a dental benefit, usually once or twice a year. Dubai's mandatory basic plans generally exclude routine dental care, so cover depends on your employer's plan.

FAQ:
Q: How much is teeth cleaning in Dubai?
A: Indicative private-clinic prices are AED 250 to 800 for a scale and polish, AED 400 to 1,000 for AirFlow, AED 350 to 1,000 for a check-up with cleaning and X-rays, and AED 200 to 750 per quadrant for deep cleaning.
Q: Does insurance in Dubai cover a scale and polish?
A: Employer plans with a dental benefit often cover one or two cleanings a year. The basic mandatory plan generally does not. Ask the clinic to check your cover before the visit.
Q: Is AirFlow better than a normal cleaning?
A: AirFlow removes stain and soft plaque well, and some people find it more comfortable. Hard tartar may still need an ultrasonic scaler. Both are acceptable ways to clean teeth; ask what your gums need.
Q: How often should I get my teeth cleaned?
A: Every six months suits most people. Your dentist may suggest every three to four months if you have gum disease or build tartar quickly, or a longer gap if your gums are healthy.

## Emergency Dentist in Dubai
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/dubai/services/emergency-dentist/

Phone before you travel. Describe the problem, ask whether a dentist can see you today and ask the consultation fee, including any out-of-hours surcharge. Opening hours vary between clinics, and some open late in the evening or at weekends, so use the clinic's own phone line to confirm.

Dubai traffic at peak hours can add half an hour to a journey across the city, so the nearest clinic that can see you is usually the better choice than a preferred clinic further away. Bring your Emirates ID, insurance card and a list of any medicines you take.

For a knocked-out adult tooth, hold it by the crown, put it back in the socket straight away if you can, or keep it in milk, and get to a dentist within 30 minutes. Go to a hospital emergency department or call 998 if swelling spreads towards the eye or neck, you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, or there is a serious facial injury.

Insurance: Emergency treatment to relieve pain or control infection is the dental care most often covered, including under some basic plans. Follow-up work is usually assessed separately. Dubai's mandatory basic plans generally exclude routine dental care, so cover depends on your employer's plan.

FAQ:
Q: Can I get an emergency dentist in Dubai on a Friday or Sunday?
A: Some private clinics open at weekends and some open late in the evening, but hours vary. Phone the clinic to confirm before you travel. For serious swelling or trauma, hospital emergency departments are open around the clock.
Q: How much does an emergency dentist cost in Dubai?
A: Indicative private-clinic prices are AED 200 to 800 for the consultation and X-ray. Treatment on the day costs extra: AED 300 to 1,500 for pain relief or draining an abscess, or AED 400 to 1,200 for a simple extraction.
Q: What should I do if a tooth is knocked out?
A: Hold it by the crown, not the root. Rinse briefly if dirty and put it back in the socket if you can, or keep it in milk. Get to a dentist within 30 minutes. Do not replant a baby tooth.
Q: Will my Dubai insurance cover emergency dental care?
A: Emergency treatment to relieve pain or treat infection is the dental care most often covered, including under the basic plan. Follow-up treatment may not be covered. Check your policy and ask the clinic about direct billing.
Q: When should I go to hospital instead of a dentist?
A: Go to a hospital emergency department or call 998 if swelling is spreading to your eye or neck, you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, bleeding will not stop, or you have a serious injury to the face or head.

## Children's Dentistry in Dubai
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/dubai/services/pediatric-dentistry/

In Dubai, children are seen by specialist pediatric dentists and by family dentists. For routine check-ups a family dentist is usually fine. For very young, anxious or medically complex children, or treatment that may need sedation, a pediatric dentist is trained for that work.

After-school and weekend appointments go quickly, so book the next check-up as you leave. Ask whether a parent can stay in the room and how the clinic handles a nervous first visit.

If your child needs extensive treatment, a clinic may suggest sedation or a general anaesthetic. Ask where it would be done, who gives the anaesthetic, and for a written estimate that includes hospital or facility fees.

Insurance: Family plans with dental benefits usually include children's check-ups and basic treatment. Dubai's mandatory basic plans generally exclude routine dental care, so cover depends on your employer's plan.

FAQ:
Q: How much is a children's dentist in Dubai?
A: Indicative private-clinic prices are AED 200 to 500 for a check-up, AED 100 to 300 for fluoride varnish, AED 150 to 400 per tooth for sealants and AED 300 to 900 for a baby-tooth filling. Treatment under general anaesthetic can cost AED 4,000 to 15,000 including facility fees.
Q: Do I need a specialist pediatric dentist in Dubai?
A: For routine check-ups a family dentist is fine. For very young, anxious or medically complex children, or treatment that may need sedation, a pediatric specialist is helpful. You can check the licence category on the DHA register.
Q: When should my child first see a dentist?
A: When the first tooth appears or by the first birthday, as advised by the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry. Early visits are short and help the child get used to the clinic.
Q: Does family insurance in Dubai cover children's dental care?
A: Plans with a dental benefit often cover check-ups and basic treatment for children. The basic mandatory plan generally does not include routine dental care. Check your policy wording.

## Wisdom Tooth Removal in Dubai
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/dubai/services/wisdom-tooth-removal/

An X-ray, and sometimes a CBCT scan, shows whether a wisdom tooth needs a simple or a surgical extraction. Ask for the quote after the scan, because the price depends on how the tooth is positioned and how close it sits to the nerve.

Impacted wisdom teeth in Dubai are removed by oral surgeons and by general dentists with surgical experience. If the tooth is deeply buried or close to the nerve, ask whether an oral and maxillofacial surgeon will do it.

Book surgical removal before a weekend or a few quieter days at work, because swelling usually peaks on day two or three. If you want all four removed at once under sedation, ask whether that suits your case and where the sedation will be given.

Insurance: Surgical treatment is covered by some dental benefits when it is medically necessary, often with pre-approval. Implants in particular are frequently excluded or capped. Dubai's mandatory basic plans generally exclude routine dental care, so cover depends on your employer's plan.

FAQ:
Q: How much is wisdom tooth removal in Dubai?
A: Indicative private-clinic prices are AED 500 to 1,500 for a simple extraction, AED 1,200 to 3,000 for surgical removal of a partly erupted tooth and AED 2,000 to 4,500 for a tooth impacted in bone. IV sedation adds AED 1,000 to 3,000.
Q: Do I need an oral surgeon in Dubai to remove a wisdom tooth?
A: Not always. General dentists remove straightforward wisdom teeth. For deeply impacted teeth or teeth close to the nerve, an oral surgeon is often recommended. You can check the licence category on the DHA register.
Q: How many days off work do I need?
A: Expect to take one to three days off after surgical removal. Swelling usually peaks around day two or three. A simple extraction often needs no more than the rest of the day.
Q: Does insurance in Dubai cover wisdom tooth removal?
A: It depends on your plan. Employer plans with a dental benefit often cover medically necessary removal with pre-approval. The basic plan generally covers only emergency care.

## Dental Crowns in Dubai
URL: https://www.appointpanda.ae/dubai/services/dental-crowns/

Some Dubai clinics mill crowns on site and fit them the same day, while others send the work to a dental lab, which means a temporary crown for one to two weeks. Same-day crowns are convenient if you are short of time; lab-made crowns may suit front teeth where shade matching is harder.

Ask which material the dentist recommends for this tooth and why. Zirconia is very strong for back teeth, while E.max and layered porcelain are often chosen for front teeth. Check whether a core build-up or post (AED 300 to 1,200) is needed and included.

If the crown follows a root canal, ask for both to be priced together and whether the same dentist will do both. Ask what the guarantee covers if the crown chips or comes loose.

Insurance: Restorative work such as fillings, root canals and crowns is commonly part of a dental benefit, with a co-payment and an annual limit. Crowns are sometimes covered at a lower rate. Dubai's mandatory basic plans generally exclude routine dental care, so cover depends on your employer's plan.

FAQ:
Q: How much is a dental crown in Dubai?
A: Indicative private-clinic prices per crown are AED 1,200 to 2,500 for porcelain fused to metal, AED 1,500 to 3,500 for zirconia, AED 1,800 to 4,500 for E.max and AED 1,800 to 4,000 for a same-day milled crown.
Q: Which is better, zirconia or E.max?
A: Zirconia is stronger and often used on back teeth and for people who grind. E.max is more translucent and often chosen for front teeth. Your dentist should explain the choice for each tooth.
Q: Can I get a same-day crown in Dubai?
A: Some clinics mill crowns on site and fit them in one visit of a few hours. Ask when booking whether the clinic has this option and whether it suits your tooth.
Q: Does insurance in Dubai cover crowns?
A: Employer plans with a dental benefit often cover crowns needed to restore a damaged tooth, with pre-approval and a co-payment. The basic plan generally does not. Crowns for appearance alone are rarely covered.
